subject: Atlas Payments POC — success criteria & KPIs (latency, throughput, cost, quality)
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Lee <sophie.lee@atlaspayments.com>, Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@atlaspayments.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 22 May 2029 15:00:00 -0700
Subject: Atlas Payments POC — success criteria & KPIs (latency, throughput, cost, quality)

Hi Sophie / Tom —

Great to speak earlier — appreciate you walking through the primary goals for the payments inbox triage POC. As promised, here’s a concise post-call recap and a proposed evaluation plan so we can lock timelines and owners. Please flag anything that’s off.

Summary of problem/opportunity
- Atlas needs faster, more accurate routing and triage for transaction disputes and refund requests to reduce MTTR and manual handling.
- Primary constraint: must run in your VPC and meet <200ms p95 latency for single-turn routing decisions.

Proposed POC scope (2 weeks sandbox + 2 weeks trial load)
- Data: 10k anonymized tickets (sample), 3 months of historical labels provided by Atlas.
- Workloads: real-time triage API (preferred) and batch nightly reprocessing.
- Goals: validate latency, throughput, cost per token, and quality against success criteria below.

Success criteria / KPIs (suggested)
- Latency: p95 inference latency <= 200ms (single request, 256-token avg).
- Throughput: sustain 1,000 requests/sec with 95% of requests served under latency SLO during steady-state load.
- Cost: average cost/token <= $0.0005 measured over trial volume (tokens in + generated tokens).
- Quality: intent classification F1 >= 0.92 on your labeled validation set; top-1 routing accuracy >= 0.90.
- Reliability: <1% error-rate and 99.9% availability during trial window.

Evaluation plan / measurements
- Redwood will run instrumented trials capturing token counts, per-request latency histograms, throughput, error-rates, and model confidence.
- Atlas provides a held-out labeled validation set and ground-truth routing decisions for quality metrics.
- We will run:
  1) Baseline inference against 1,000 sample requests to calibrate latency.
  2) Ramp test to 1k RPS for throughput + autoscaling validation.
  3) Cost run over 100k requests to measure cost/token and projected monthly cost.

Ownership and deliverables
- Jordan Blake (Sales) — POC owner, schedules runs, primary contact for timelines and escalations.
- Neha Kapoor (SE) — technical lead for integration, telemetry, and SSO/KMS checks.
- Marissa Cole (CS/Success) — success criteria verification, quality measurement, and adoption playbook.
- Atlas: Sophie (Product) — provides dataset, labels, and acceptance criteria; Tom (Infra) — VPC details, network allowlists, and service account.

Tentative timeline
- May 27: Data handoff + SSO/KMS onboarding
- May 29–31: Sandbox run (sanity, latency checks)
- Jun 3–7: Trial load (throughput+cost measurements)
- Jun 10: POC review + acceptance decision

Attachments: redwood_poc_plan.pdf (high-level POC plan), slo_template.xlsx (SLO & metrics template).

Next steps
1) Sophie — confirm data readiness and whether a sample can be uploaded to the shared Drive by Mon (May 27).
2) Tom — confirm VPC peering/allowlist details and whether we need an on-prem package.
3) Redwood (Neha) — prepare integration checklist and test account.

Thanks — will follow up to lock the first-run window once you confirm dates.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192

From: Sophie Lee <sophie.lee@atlaspayments.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@atlaspayments.com>
Date: Thu, 23 May 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Atlas Payments POC — success criteria & KPIs (latency, throughput, cost, quality)

Thanks Jordan — this looks good and aligned with what we discussed. A few clarifications:
- We can provide a 12k row anonymized dataset and a 2k labeled validation set by EOD May 27. Sophie will upload to the Drive link.
- For latency: the 200ms p95 is our target for cold-start tolerant performance; happy to evaluate with a 256-token average.
- Throughput: 1k RPS is our peak concurrently for the busiest windows — we care most about steady-state, but will want an autoscaling demonstration.
- Cost: the $0.0005/token target is aspirational; we want Redwood to show projections and potential levers (batching/quantization).

On ownership: Tom will coordinate with our infra team for allowlist details. Tom — can you confirm whether we need a transient VPN or if VPC peering is fine?

We’re good to proceed on the proposed timeline; please put the May 29 sandbox slot on the calendar.

Best,
Sophie
Senior Product Manager | Atlas Payments
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Lee <sophie.lee@atlaspayments.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@atlaspayments.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 23 May 2029 11:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Atlas Payments POC — success criteria & KPIs (latency, throughput, cost, quality)

Hi Sophie / Tom —

Thanks for the quick confirmation. Technical notes / checklist from our side:
- Integration: we’ll provide a small SDK and a swagger for the triage endpoint; will need a service account and allowlist IPs.
- Telemetry: plan to send per-request traces to the Drive link as CSV + provide dashboards in the Redwood Console for p50/p95/p99 latency, RPS, token counts, and error-rate.
- Autoscaling: we’ll demonstrate horizontal autoscaling with graceful degradation to a smaller model variant if capacity is constrained — we will log fallbacks to the Console.

Tests we’ll run during the trial:
1) Latency baseline (1k sample) — measure p50/p95/p99.
2) Throughput ramp: 100 -> 500 -> 1k RPS, 15 minutes each, monitoring queue depth and tail latency.
3) Cost projection run: 100k requests to capture average tokens/request and compute cost/token.

I’ve attached the SLO template (slo_template.xlsx) filled with our recommended thresholds and measurement windows.

Action items assigned:
- Atlas (Sophie): upload dataset to Drive (by 2029-05-27).
- Atlas (Tom): provide service account + allowlist info (by 2029-05-28).
- Redwood (Neha): share SDK + integration guide by 2029-05-24 and schedule sandbox run.
- Redwood (Marissa): prepare acceptance checklist and success criteria dashboard for the review on Jun 10.

Let us know if you want us to reduce the default token window for the latency test (we can run both 128 and 256 token baselines).

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Lee <sophie.lee@atlaspayments.com>
Cc: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@atlaspayments.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 24 May 2029 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Atlas Payments POC — success criteria & KPIs (latency, throughput, cost, quality)

Perfect — thanks everyone for the quick alignment. I’ve tentatively scheduled the sandbox slot for May 29 (09:00 PT) and invited the Redwood and Atlas technical leads. I’ll upload the filled POC plan to the shared Drive and ping when the SDK is ready.

One quick operational ask: Sophie, can you confirm whether the validation labels include both intent and routing target (yes/no)? We’ll need both for the F1/top-1 accuracy metrics.

If nothing else, we’ll use the following acceptance gates for the Jun 10 review:
- Latency p95 <= 200ms (256 token baseline)
- Top-1 routing accuracy >= 90% on your validation set
- Cost/token projection <= $0.0005 with suggested optimizations called out

If any of these look unachievable during the trial, we’ll capture a remediation plan and a proposal for next steps (model/quantization recommendations, batching settings).

Thanks — looking forward to the run.

Jordan
